intro: A five course menu built around mushrooms, with each course labelled by how it is cooked: baked, sautéed, grilled and baked again for dessert. Trumpet, chanterelle, lion's mane, portabella and porcini all appear, and the last course puts porcini into chocolate. The optional wine pairing adds $55.

courses.name: Trumpet Mushroom Fritter
courses.tableside: A one bite amuse to open the menu: king trumpet mushroom in a light fritter batter, with lemon aioli. The trumpet comes back again on the lion's mane course.

shellfish.note: Fried. Confirm whether the fryer is shared with shellfish.

gluten.note: Fritter batter is usually wheat flour. Confirm.

eggs.note: Aioli is egg yolk based, and batter often contains egg.

vegetarian.note: No meat or fish. Confirm the fryer for a strict vegetarian.

key_terms.definition: Pleurotus eryngii, the largest of the oyster mushrooms. The thick white stem is the main eating part and keeps a meaty, almost scallop like texture when cooked.
A Provençal emulsion of garlic and oil. Modern versions are usually built on egg yolk like a mayonnaise.

courses.chef_notes: One bite to open. Introduce the mushroom theme as it lands. Ask about the fryer for a shellfish or celiac guest.

courses.name: Chanterelle Terrine
courses.description: Spicy mustard, red wine poached prune, frisee
courses.tableside: A baked terrine of chanterelles, sliced and served with spicy mustard, a prune poached in red wine and a little frisée. Chanterelles are wild, so every one on the plate was foraged.

dairy.note: Terrines are often bound with cream. Confirm.

nuts.note: Pistachio is a common terrine garnish. Confirm none is used.

gluten.note: Terrines are sometimes bound with breadcrumb. Confirm.

eggs.note: Terrines are often bound with egg. Confirm.

vegetarian.note: Many terrines contain pork fat or are set with gelatin. Confirm this one is meat free.

key_terms.definition: A golden, funnel shaped wild mushroom with blunt ridges running down the stem instead of true gills. It cannot be reliably cultivated, so all chanterelles are foraged. Faint apricot aroma.
A loaf pressed and cooked in a straight sided mould, also called a terrine, then sliced and served cold or at room temperature.
Curly endive. Pale, crisp and bitter, used here to cut the richness.

courses.chef_notes: Confirm the binder before clearing this course for a vegetarian, dairy, egg or gluten restriction. Mustard is on the plate, so name it for a guest who asks.

pairing.name: Viura/Garnacha Blanca/Maturana Blanca Gran Reserva Blanco, Rioja
pairing.note: A Gran Reserva white Rioja with ten years behind it, which means at least four years of ageing before release with six months in oak. That age turns the fruit nutty and savoury, and it sits right on top of the earthy chanterelle. Its acidity cuts the richness of the terrine and the spicy mustard, and the dried fruit character from long ageing links to the red wine poached prune. A young, fruity white would taste thin next to this course.

courses.name: Wild Mushroom Tortellini
courses.description: Truffle cream, fried sage, parmesan tuille
courses.tableside: Tortellini filled with sautéed wild mushrooms, in a truffle cream with fried sage leaves and a crisp parmesan tuile on top.

eggs.note: Fresh pasta dough is normally made with egg. Confirm.

vegetarian.note: No meat expected. Parmesan is traditionally made with animal rennet, which matters to a strict vegetarian.

key_terms.definition: Small ring shaped stuffed pasta from Emilia, around Bologna and Modena.
French for tile. A thin, curved crisp wafer, here baked from parmesan alone.
Cream sauce flavoured with truffle. Truffles are underground fungi, cousins of the mushrooms on the rest of the menu.

courses.chef_notes: Cannot be made gluten or dairy free. For a strict vegetarian, raise the parmesan rennet question rather than clearing the course outright.

pairing.name: Vigna San Carlo, Pinot Nero
pairing.note: Light bodied Pinot Noir with red fruit and an earthy, forest floor side that runs straight into the wild mushrooms. Low tannin means the truffle cream doesn't turn it bitter, and its acidity cuts through the cream and parmesan. Saracco is best known for Moscato d'Asti, which makes this single vineyard Pinot Nero an unusual bottle from them.

courses.name: Lion's Mane Mushroom Steak
courses.description: Mushroom ketchup, grilled portabella, trumpet mushroom, blue Stilton
courses.tableside: Lion's mane cut thick and grilled like a steak, with grilled portabella, king trumpet, a house mushroom ketchup and blue Stilton. The main course, and meaty enough to stand in for one.

dairy.note: Blue Stilton. Ask whether it can be left off.

gluten.note: Mushroom ketchup recipes often include Worcestershire or soy sauce, which can carry wheat. Confirm.

vegetarian.note: Traditional English mushroom ketchup sometimes includes anchovy. Confirm the house version, and Stilton rennet for a strict vegetarian.

key_terms.definition: Hericium erinaceus, a white mushroom that grows in shaggy cascading spines. Seared, it has a texture people compare to crab or lobster.
An eighteenth century English condiment of salted mushrooms cooked down with spices. Ketchup originally meant a savoury sauce, and tomato came later.
An English blue cheese with protected status. It can only be made in Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire, which rules out the village of Stilton itself.

courses.chef_notes: The vegetarian main of the menu in effect, but confirm the mushroom ketchup before calling it vegetarian.

pairing.name: Merlot/Cab Franc/Cab Sauv/Malbec, St-Émilion
pairing.grapes: Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec
pairing.note: Merlot-led Right Bank Bordeaux with soft tannin, plum fruit and an earthy side that suits a meaty mushroom course. The char from the grill wants a red with some structure, and the Stilton's salt and blue funk soften the tannin. Six years of age have turned the fruit toward savoury, which suits the mushroom ketchup.

courses.name: Porcini Chocolate Truffle
courses.description: Porcini chocolate ganache, cocoa nib, porcini vanilla creme, toasted cashew
courses.tableside: Dessert keeps the theme: a chocolate truffle with porcini in the ganache, cocoa nib, a porcini and vanilla crème and toasted cashews. Dried porcini taste nutty and savoury, which works with dark chocolate the way salt does.

dairy.note: Ganache and crème are cream based.

nuts.note: Toasted cashews are on the plate. Ask whether they can be left off.

gluten.note: Confirm whether there is any biscuit or flour component.

eggs.note: Confirm whether the crème uses egg yolk.

soy.note: Chocolate often contains soy lecithin. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: Boletus edulis, the king bolete. Dried porcini have an intense nutty, savoury aroma.
Chocolate melted into warm cream, the base of a truffle.
Roasted, crushed cacao bean before it is ground into chocolate. Crunchy and bitter with no added sugar.

courses.chef_notes: Cashew is a tree nut and is on the plate. Confirm whether it can be held before offering the course to a nut allergic guest.

pairing.name: 10 Year Old Tawny Port
pairing.grapes: Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca and other Douro varieties
pairing.note: Ten year tawny, aged in small oak casks until the fruit turns to hazelnut, fig and dried cherry. Dow's makes a drier style of port than most houses, which keeps a chocolate dessert from tipping into too much sugar. The nutty character matches the toasted cashew and the savoury porcini, and the dried fruit sits with the cocoa nib. Our regular afters list carries Graham's tawnies instead, so this is a tasting menu pour.
